chosen.premise: Cleaner environments made Muk so rare that sludge ponds are being built to prevent its extinction.
chosen.hook: Cleaning up the world may be driving Muk extinct.
chosen.visualIdea: Contrast a cleaned-up city with an empty Muk habitat, then reveal purpose-built sludge ponds.
chosen.note: A compelling ecological contradiction unique to Muk: environmental improvement reduces its habitat, while sludge ponds are built to save it. Multiple entries support the premise and provide a clear narrative arc.

candidates.premise: Everywhere Muk moves can become barren for three years because its poison leaks into the ground.
candidates.hook: Muk can leave a three-year wasteland just by walking.
candidates.visualIdea: Animate healthy grass turning barren behind Muk, then add a three-year countdown.
candidates.note: A striking, precise consequence with excellent visual potential. It relies on one Pokédex entry, so the claim has less corroboration than the strongest angles.

candidates.premise: A single drop of Muk's body fluid can turn an entire pool stagnant and rancid.
candidates.hook: One drop of Muk can ruin a whole pool.
candidates.visualIdea: Drop one glowing blob into clear water and rapidly transform the pool into rancid sludge.
candidates.note: The single-drop-to-ruined-pool scale is memorable and highly visual. It is strongly stated in one entry but lacks additional supporting evidence.

candidates.premise: Muk smells bad enough to make people faint, yet degeneration made it lose its sense of smell.
candidates.hook: Muk is so disgusting that it evolved past being able to smell it.
candidates.visualIdea: Show Muk emitting stink waves, a fainting person, then zoom into Muk's vanished nose.
candidates.note: A highly Muk-specific contradiction, directly supported by multiple Pokédex entries. The vanished sense of smell is visually suggestive, though the causal wording may need careful framing.

candidates.premise: Muk does not just poison what touches it—its footprints contain poison too.
candidates.visualIdea: Track Muk walking across the ground as each footprint glows toxic and poisons the path.
candidates.note: Extremely concrete and easy to visualize, with direct support. It is slightly less surprising because it is an extension of Muk’s general toxicity.

candidates.premise: Alolan Muk is shorter than Muk but weighs 22 kilograms more and gains the Dark type.
candidates.hook: Alolan Muk is shorter, yet weighs 22 kilos more.
candidates.visualIdea: Place both forms side by side with height and weight bars, then reveal Alolan Muk's extra type.
candidates.note: The 22-kilogram difference is precise, verifiable, and easy to display. However, comparison angles are less inherently dramatic than Muk’s toxic ecology.

rounds.request: None needed; the chosen angle is well supported. A stronger alternative would need an equally specific contradiction or extreme consequence with multiple supporting entries.
